J U D G M E N T Thottathil B.Radhakrishnan, J.
1.Private respondents served.
They do not appear to oppose the writ petition.
2.Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Senior Government Pleader.
Petitioner seeks an order of police protection for his proprietary concern, which is shown to be functioning with due licences.
A crime has already been registered against the private respondents for an incident which allegedly happened on 16.10.2016 for throwing stones causing damage to the petitioner's vehicles.
Petitioner's unit was apparently attempted to be attacked under the premise that it causes pollution.
With the available materials and certificates, the petitioner is entitled to carry out the WP(C)37368/16 activities.

He has the requisite licence from the Grama Panchayat,
integrated consent to operate issued by the Kerala State Pollution Control Board, licence from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and licence under the Factories and Boilers Act.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: With these materials, we are sure that this is an eminently fit case for a direction to the first respondent to accord adequate protection to the life of the petitioner and his property, including his unit "Quality Food Product Industries" at Panavally, its officials, employees, staff and workers, as also, vehicles coming there for due functioning and operations, without any threat or hindrance from respondent Nos.2 and 3, as also, their henchmen.
Insofar as the protection to the properties is concerned, the official respondent would be entitled to levy due charges, in accordance with law, as may be found necessary.
This writ petition is ordered accordingly.
(THOTTATHIL B.RADHAKRISHNAN, JUDGE) (DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN, JUDGE) jg-30/11
